summary: Task-selective product interface design guidance organized around structure, behavior, and finish.
description: Design, implement, and review clear, responsive, accessible product interfaces using the project's existing design system.
plainLanguageSummary: Use this for product screens that need better structure, behavior, or rendered finish without replacing project-owned design truth.

ownership.purpose: Improve the hierarchy, composition, language, responsive behavior, and rendered polish of product interfaces using project-owned design truth.
owns: Human interface writing and content-role economy
Responsive presentation, complete states, and rendered polish review
excludes: Generated, vendored, build, and distribution output
Public marketing narrative and conversion strategy
Business workflow design, deep security review, and data-visualization semantics
overlapRules: Load another pack only when it contributes a distinct flow, component, accessibility, performance, security, or data-interface judgment.
Project tokens, components, terminology, Actions, and Guards remain authoritative over reusable guidance.

modules.title: Structure
modules.summary: Define the interface job, reading order, information hierarchy, product language, and product-specific character before styling details.

positiveSignals.summary: The task creates or materially changes hierarchy, layout, reading order, brand expression, or user-facing language on a rendered product surface.
evidence: A Task-owned product page, screen, navigation surface, layout, or interface-content role changes

positiveSignals.summary: The task creates or materially revises labels, actions, guidance, empty states, errors, confirmations, onboarding, or settings language.
evidence: Owned rendered source or acceptance changes user-facing product language

negativeSignals.summary: The task has no rendered product-interface surface.
evidence: Owned paths and acceptance remain backend, infrastructure, generated output, or internal documentation

rubricDimensions: plain language, terminology, voice, and contextual tone
page-wide content-role uniqueness and repetition control
action labels, feedback, errors, empty states, and recovery
inclusion, user agency, and interruption discipline

modules.title: Finish
modules.summary: Apply disciplined typography, spacing, layers, attention, density, and evidence-based rendered review without generic UI treatments.

positiveSignals.summary: The task materially changes or reviews typography, spacing, alignment, surfaces, density, containment, background layers, attention hierarchy, or rendered polish.
evidence: Owned frontend source or acceptance changes a rendered page, shell, panel, component composition, visual treatment, or proof boundary

positiveSignals.summary: The task needs closure or review against rendered product-interface evidence.
evidence: Acceptance names polish, review, screenshot, visual proof, responsive proof, or interface closure

positiveSignals.summary: The task applies project tokens or components to the rendered composition and visual system.
evidence: Acceptance names semantic tokens, component defaults, design-system conformance, or a local palette

negativeSignals.summary: The task is a mechanical rename or generated-output refresh with no rendered composition change.
evidence: Acceptance requires no visual, responsive, hierarchy, or interaction behavior change

rubricDimensions: surface, border, elevation, and density discipline

modules.title: Behavior
modules.summary: Implement responsive interaction, complete states, accessible behavior, component reuse, and narrow framework boundaries.

positiveSignals.summary: The task changes responsive layout, interactive controls, component composition, or user input behavior.
evidence: Acceptance or owned source changes viewport adaptation, navigation, controls, overlays, forms, data display, or user interaction

positiveSignals.summary: The task changes a client or server rendering boundary, hydration behavior, or interactive island.
evidence: Acceptance names hydration, a client or server boundary, a rendering directive, or an interactive island

positiveSignals.summary: The task changes responsive layout or interaction across narrow, intermediate, and wide content constraints.
evidence: Acceptance names responsive transformation, viewport adaptation, reordering, overlays, or scroll ownership

positiveSignals.summary: The task implements asynchronous rendering or control availability across loading, empty, failure, permission, success, disabled, and retry conditions.
evidence: Owned source changes rendered lifecycle conditions or their interactive recovery behavior

negativeSignals.summary: The task changes no responsive or stateful product behavior.
evidence: The rendered output is fixed, generated, or outside a user workflow

negativeSignals.summary: The task changes interface wording only and does not alter interactive behavior, component structure, state transitions, or responsive layout.
evidence: The Task explicitly limits work to labels, messages, guidance, or other user-facing copy

rubricDimensions: component reuse, ownership, API shape, and durable naming

failureSignals.summary: Agents repeatedly apply a composition suited to a different product job, density, risk, or interaction model.
Visual precedent repeatedly comes from a homepage, unrelated archetype, viewport, or state and does not support the implemented decision.
Color repeatedly decorates the interface without preserving distinct action, focus, semantic, data, neutral, or brand-expression meaning.
Saturated backgrounds, borders, icons, badges, dots, links, metadata, and status text repeatedly compete instead of preserving one clear attention order.
Page tint, nested surfaces, borders, or elevation repeatedly obscure the canvas and persistent layer hierarchy or make unused background dominate the task.
Interfaces repeatedly default to a generic dark shell, tinted canvas, bordered cards, pills, and permanent sidebar-list-inspector composition without same-task project evidence.
Screens repeatedly converge on interchangeable gradient, oversized-heading, icon-card, pill, generic-accent, or fake-metric styling without project evidence.
Raw color, spacing, radius, or shadow values recur where project tokens exist.
Small interactive behavior repeatedly expands the client-rendered component tree.
Interfaces repeatedly expose technical terms, duplicate headings, vague actions, robotic language, dead ends, or unnecessary explanatory text.
Desktop layouts repeatedly compress or overflow instead of adapting to content and interaction constraints.
Type roles, spacing rhythm, alignment, or density repeatedly obscure the page's primary reading order.
Nested cards, borders, shadows, pills, or competing surfaces repeatedly replace whitespace and hierarchy.
Bounded content, scrolling, navigation state, focus, or persistent controls repeatedly fail in the rendered interface.
Agents repeatedly create components, wrappers, or variants that duplicate an existing semantic role or extension point.
Component, prop, or variant names repeatedly mirror temporary request wording, visual treatment, motion, or feature-local adjectives instead of durable roles.
Shell, breadcrumb, eyebrow, title, description, navigation, and panel copy repeatedly compete for the same language role.
